# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P88](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0088), [v5 c1 P8](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0008)</sub>
- **Status:** Unmarried  <sub>[v5 c11 P5](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0005), [v5 c15 P32](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0032)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper and maid-of-all-work at Ingleside  <sub>[v4 c18 P57](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0057), [v5 c1 P1](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan is a tall, grim-faced, and elderly spinster with a plain appearance and a dark complexion. She acknowledges her own lack of conventional beauty, but takes pride in her neatness and capable hands.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P57](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0057), [v4 c25 P16](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0016), [v4 c35 P5](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0005), [v5 c1 P1](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0001)_

## Personality

Susan is fiercely loyal, deeply religious, and intensely devoted to the Blythe family, particularly Anne and her children. Though she often speaks her mind with sharp, humorous candor and harbors strong prejudices against Methodists and bad housekeeping, she is fundamentally kind-hearted and maternal. She takes great pride in her domestic culinary skills and approaches her household duties with uncompromising thoroughness.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P57](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0057), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c34 P17](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0017), [v4 c40 P6](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0006), [v5 c1 P6](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0006), [v5 c15 P22](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0022)_

## Goals

- To serve and care for the Blythe family at Ingleside  <sub>[v4 c40 P43](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0043), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007)</sub>

## History

Susan Baker originally entered the service of Gilbert and Anne Blythe as a maid-of-all-work at their first home, the 'house of dreams' near Four Winds Harbor. When Anne suffered from a prolonged illness following the birth of her son Shirley, Susan stepped in to nurse and hand-rear the infant, forming a lifelong maternal bond with him. She subsequently relocated with the family to their permanent home, Ingleside, in Glen St. Mary. Throughout the years, she managed the household with tireless energy, cooked indefatigably for the family, and stoutly defended the Blythe children and Mr. Meredith's neglected family against local gossip. During an absence when she went to care for her sister Matilda, who had broken her leg, she temporarily yielded her kitchen duties to Leslie Moore, but returned as soon as possible to resume her position as the undisputed helm of the Ingleside household.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P57](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0057), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c40 P43](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0043), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007), [v5 c7 P17](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0017)_

## Quotes

> I gave him life just as much as you did, Mrs. Dr. dear. He is just as much my baby as he is yours.  <sub>[v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005)</sub>

> There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

> It is a very strange world, Mrs. Doctor, dear. But maybe I will have a chance to get married yet.  <sub>[v4 c22 P9](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0009)</sub>

> Cornelia Elliott thinks she was born to run this world, Mrs. Dr. dear, and so she is always in a stew over something. I have never thought I was, and so I go calmly along.  <sub>[v5 c26 P9](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0009)</sub>

> I have been hearing of Amelia Warren’s weak heart for forty years... She enjoys making a fuss and having the doctor, and any excuse will do.  <sub>[v5 c7 P24](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0024)</sub>
